title: Malicious Dependencies
overview: Investigate a dependency review that added a lifecycle hook and lost expected provenance.
prerequisites: Know the basics of CI/CD auditing and how to review authorization context.

attack.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: A new package version with an installation hook and missing provenance merits a review before approving a build.
evidence: Compare lockfile diff, package identity, introduced hook metadata and publisher assertions.
false_positive: A legitimate dependency may add build-time setup before enabling provenance.
tuning: Approve package changes by version and registry identity. Maintain a recovery strategy for pinning older versions.
response: Pause the update, preserve the diff, verify upstream provenance and review existing builds for the version.
prevention: Use dependency review, pinned lockfiles, restricted install scripts and verified provenance.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: No package is fetched or run during replay. The event summarizes review metadata only.

options: New install hook and missing provenance
Any change in lockfile line count
questions.explanation: Both behavior and provenance affect build trust.

questions.prompt: What should be inspected before approval?
options: Package identity, source and lockfile diff
questions.explanation: Review the precise version and its intended behavior.
